lessonRef.subject: mathematics
lessonRef.title: Applied problem solving: connecting geometry, fractions, and measurement

sections.title: Instructional examples
sections.directions: This example shows the kind of reasoning the problem below asks for.

items.prompt: A rectangular patio is 7 m long and 4 m wide. What is its area?

sections.title: Guided practice
sections.directions: Talk through what the problem is asking before you compute.

items.prompt: A garden bed is divided into 6 equal sections. 2 sections are planted with flowers. What fraction of the bed is planted?
A square garden plot is partitioned into 6 parts of equal area. What fraction of the plot does one part represent?

sections.title: Independent practice
sections.directions: Work on your own. Show the steps that produced each answer.

items.prompt: A rectangular patio is 6 ft long and 8 ft wide. What is its area?
A garden bed is divided into 8 equal sections. 2 sections are planted with flowers. What fraction of the bed is planted?
A square garden plot is partitioned into 8 parts of equal area. What fraction of the plot does one part represent?

sections.title: Extension and challenge
sections.directions: Write out the reasoning in full sentences. A correct answer with no justification does not count here.

items.prompt: A rectangular patio is 8 ft long and 12 ft wide. What is its area?
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.

items.prompt: A garden bed is divided into 8 equal sections. 3 sections are planted with flowers. What fraction of the bed is planted?
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.
